title: APS 06 – One-dimensional data structures
description: Midterm 1 theory: stacks, queues, cyclic arrays, priority queues, postfix notation.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about a stack?

options.text: It can only be implemented with a doubly linked list

questions.question: A stack is a one-dimensional linear sequence of elements that works by the principle:
Adding new elements to and removing them from the stack:

options.text: depends on how full the stack is

questions.question: When implementing a stack with a linked list, adding and removing an element is done:

options.text: At the start of the list
At the end of the list
At an arbitrary location in the list
In the middle of the list

questions.question: What is the complexity of adding (push) / removing (pop) an element in a stack implemented with an array?
Implementing a stack with a list:

options.text: The middle element of the list is the top of the stack
The first element of the list is the top of the stack, but the stack has a fixed maximum size
The first element of the list is the top of the stack, and the stack is unbounded
The last element of the list is the top of the stack, and the stack is bounded

questions.question: A stack implemented with an array:

options.text: Is unbounded, it grows as needed
Adds and removes elements at index 0, shifting the rest
Has a limited length that depends on the length of the array (maxdepth)

questions.question: To most efficiently solve the problem of checking for well-placed brackets in arithmetic expressions, you use:

options.text: none of the offered abstract data structures

questions.question: Which of the following is the best solution for reversing the order of elements?
If the elements "A", "B", "C" and "D" are inserted into an empty queue, in what order will they be removed?
What is a queue?

options.text: A one-dimensional linear sequence of elements that works by the last-in-first-out (LIFO) principle
A sequence where elements are always removed by priority
A one-dimensional linear sequence of elements that works by the first-in-first-out (FIFO) principle: added at the tail, removed from the head
A sequence where elements are added and removed only at the head

questions.question: When an element is inserted into a queue, it's inserted at the ____ of the queue, with the operation ____.
Which operation is used to remove the element at the head (start) of a queue?
If a queue is implemented with an SLL, removing an element from the queue is done with which SLL method?

options.text: Deleting the element at the start of the SLL
Deleting the element at the end of the SLL
Inserting an element at the start of the SLL
Deleting an element in the middle of the SLL

questions.question: How many stacks are needed to implement a queue?
When implementing a queue with an array, the elements are located (e = array, f = head, r = tail) between:
What is a cyclic array used for?

options.text: In sorting, to merge two halves
In a stack, so it never overflows
In a sparse matrix, to store only the non-zero values
In a queue, so the elements don't have to be shifted: a[0] comes after a[n−1]

questions.question: In a queue implemented with a singly linked list, if only the front pointer is kept, which of the following operations has the worst running time?

options.text: Both adding an element and deleting the whole queue

questions.question: In a priority queue, the largest (highest priority) element:
What is the worst-case complexity of inserting an element into a priority queue?
In a priority queue implemented with a sorted SLL, what are the complexities of inserting and removing an element?
What is the complexity of adding, and of removing, an element from a priority queue implemented with a sorted array?
What is true for a priority queue represented with an unsorted array?

options.text: Adding an element O(1), removing an element O(n)
Adding an element O(n), removing an element O(1)
Adding and removing are both O(1)
Adding and removing are both O(log n)

questions.question: If we want to use an abstract data type (ADT) in our application, we need to:

options.text: Implement it with an array first
Specify the set of values and the operations on those values (without saying how they're implemented)
Choose the programming language and the memory layout of the data
Specify only its implementation, not its operations

options.text: The operator is pushed onto the stack
